fields.notes: MISSING as a distinct column. 'My requests' matching is `ticket.requester === session.user.email` (panes.tsx:707), so any ticket created from the agent side with a display name never appears for its requester.

fields.notes: Stored as LABEL. priorityTone lookup (panes.tsx:12-17) only knows Urgent/High/Medium/Low, so a custom priority renders with `undefined` in its className.

fields.notes: MISSING. Shift handoffs copy speaks of 'a team's live tickets' (settings.tsx:1100) with no team column anywhere.

fields.name: updatedAt

fields.name: closedAt
fields.notes: MISSING; Resolved and Closed currently share resolvedAt.

fields.notes: MISSING. The SLA report prints a 'First-response met' column (panes.tsx:920) computed from !slaBreached — no first-response timestamp exists anywhere.

Label not id; MyRequests writes 'Other', absent from the default set.
Label not id; MyRequests writes 'Portal' which matches no channel label.

openQuestions: CSAT scale is contradictory in the source and must be decided, not guessed: the settings input for 'Low-score threshold' is min=1 max=5 and the dashboard averages a number to one decimal, but the 'What the customer sees' panel offers only 'Thumbs Up / Thumbs Down' (settings.tsx:523-533 vs 592-600). Is CSAT a 1–5 rating, a binary satisfied/not, or a 5-point scale presented as two buttons?

Is NPS per-ticket or per-relationship, and what triggers it? The review-queue copy claims 'every NPS detractor (0–6)' joins the low-score queue and a report tab is named NPS, but no model, survey, cadence or capture surface exists anywhere (settings.tsx:734-736, supportData.ts:62).

What exactly starts and stops an SLA clock? Statuses carry a 'waiting — SLA paused' behaviour but nothing pauses anything. Confirm: does the clock pause for the whole time in a waiting status, resume on the next active status, and is the first-response clock separate from the resolution clock?

What counts as a 'first response'? The SLA report prints a First-response column but no first-response timestamp exists. Is it the first public outbound agent message only, or does an auto-response satisfy it?
How is 'reopen' defined for the Reopen Rate report — any transition from a closed-behaviour status back to an active one, only within N days of resolution, or only customer-initiated reopens?

Should the SLA detector measure from ticket creation (as the prototype does) or from the last customer reply / last status change? The current sweep uses createdAt with no business hours (settings.tsx:1048-1052).

Auto-close currently reuses the CSAT 'Skip tickets older than (days)' value as its window (settings.tsx:1057). Is that intentional, or does auto-close need its own configurable window — and must a ticket awaiting a CSAT response be exempt?

Which entitlement actually gates SLA Policies and Routing Rules? Today the gate is a hardcoded constant map, not a plan record, and there is no implementation behind it. Confirm whether these ship, and in which plan tier.

Ticket reference scheme: is SUP-0001 per tenant, per company or global, does it reset annually, and what is the format beyond 9999? The prototype derives it from array length, which is neither gap-free nor collision-safe.
Should tickets be scoped to a legal entity (Company) as well as a tenant? The workspace models multiple companies and intercompany pairs, but a ticket carries no company reference at all.

Service tier → SLA policy resolution is by display NAME today ('create a policy called "Platinum"'). Confirm this becomes a foreign key, and decide the behaviour when a mapped policy is renamed or deleted — silently fall back to the default (current behaviour) or block the change?
Where does a customer's service tier live? The Tiers pane says 'Set a customer's tier on their contact record', but support has no contact entity and no defined link to the CRM app.
Are the four service tiers (Bronze/Silver/Gold/Platinum) a fixed platform vocabulary or tenant-editable? They are a hardcoded const array today while every other taxonomy is editable.

Email provider and sending contract for CSAT surveys, auto-responses, scheduled report emails and ticket notifications — no provider, credential, sender domain, bounce handling or suppression list exists in the repository. This must be chosen explicitly; it cannot be inferred.

Inbound email: which protocol and credential model (IMAP password, OAuth app password, or a provider API), and what is the thread-matching key — RFC Message-ID/In-Reply-To/References, a reference token injected into the subject, or a per-ticket reply-to address? None is specified in source.
Inbound channel providers (SMS / WhatsApp / chat) and their webhook signature scheme, replay window and tenant-resolution strategy — unspecified; must not be invented.
Business-hours semantics: which timezone source (tenant, team or policy), what holiday-calendar format, and does a schedule attach to an SLA policy, a team, or both?

Auto-response matching: what conditions are supported (channel, category, keyword, business hours), and what is the message template/merge-field syntax? Canned responses have the same open question — 'body' has no defined variable syntax today.
Shift handoff requires a team model that does not exist. Define teams, membership, and the 'incoming team's own assignment strategy' named in the copy (round-robin, least-loaded, manual?).
Report exports offers an 'Excel' format that currently produces CSV. Is a real XLSX writer required, or should the option be removed?

Which report each scheduled export actually runs, on what cadence options, in whose timezone, and to which recipients — the current schedule row has none of these and hardcodes 'weekly / every Monday'.

Roles and permissions for support are entirely absent: every audit row is written as role 'Org_admin'. Define the role set (agent, senior agent, supervisor, admin, end user, portal user) and, specifically, who may reassign another agent's ticket, who may see internal notes, who may export, and who may edit ticket fields.
Should the 'Types' taxonomy (Question/Problem/Incident/Task/Feature Request) be applied to tickets? It is fully editable in Settings but no ticket carries a type and nothing reads it.

Tags: free-text (current behaviour) or a managed vocabulary? And should the tag filter support multiple comma-separated tags with AND or OR semantics — the placeholder says 'tag(s)' but only one needle is matched.

KB article visibility: the widget Help tab and the partner portal 'Help / KB' tab both imply public articles, but an article has only draft/published/archived with no internal-vs-public flag. Define the visibility model, and whether portal visibility is per-role.
KB multi-language: the Tiers & search copy is explicitly about a German customer and an English article. Is the KB multi-locale with translated variants of one article, or one article per locale?
Attachments: tickets, replies and KB articles have no file handling at all. Confirm whether attachments are in scope and which object store/limits/virus-scanning apply.

Widget public intake: which tenant identifier goes in the embed snippet (it is hardcoded to 'acme' today), what origin allowlist and rate limits apply, and what anti-abuse measure is acceptable for an anonymous ticket-creation endpoint.

'My requests' matches on an exact email string equality. Should requester identity be a contact record (so an agent-created ticket appears for its requester), and should portal users and internal employees share one requester identity model?

Data retention and deletion for tickets, thread messages, raw inbound messages and CSAT comments — the prototype has no delete path for tickets and truncates its audit log at 500 entries, so neither retention nor legal hold is expressed anywhere.
